title: Gina settings.json
description: Bundle runtime settings: locale, server engine, CORS response headers, file upload limits, and Socket.io config.

region.description: Locale and timezone settings for this bundle.

i18n.description: Runtime i18n configuration for the per-bundle message catalogs (bundle/locales/<culture>.json). All keys are read from the bundle's merged settings.

cookieName.description: Locale-persistence cookie name read by the per-request locale negotiation (honoured since 0.5.16). null disables cookie-based negotiation; absent or empty keeps "gina_culture".

devMissingKey.description: Dev-mode prefix marker for missing catalog keys (only applied when NODE_ENV_IS_DEV is "true"). null disables the marker.

fallbackChain.description: Optional override of the default catalog-lookup fallback chain (specific culture, then base language, then settings.region.culture, then GINA_CULTURE, then "en"). null uses the default.

cultures.description: Explicit culture allowlist for the user-signal negotiation steps (URL prefix, cookie, Accept-Language), honoured since 0.5.22: a non-empty array constrains matching to the listed cultures (staged rollouts). null or [] derives from the bundle's loaded catalogs. The bundle-default step (settings.region.culture) is never constrained.

auth.description: Authentication & authorization gate settings (#COMPLY1 route authorization + #MS3 machine-caller authentication). Boot config: changes need a bundle restart. Route-level gating itself is declared in routing.json (param.requireAuth / param.roles / param.policy).

requireAuthByDefault.description: Deny-by-default authorization (#COMPLY10) — STRICTLY boolean (any other type refuses to boot: a truthy string would leave every un-annotated route silently UNGATED). When true, every route in this bundle requires an authenticated session unless its routing.json param block carries "public": true. Routes already declaring requireAuth / roles / policy are unaffected, and "public" can never un-gate one of those. Recorded PER BUNDLE, so enabling it in one bundle never changes a sibling's posture in merged mode. Fail-closed default: false.

loginRoute.description: Login bounce target for unauthenticated BROWSER navigations on gated routes: a routing.json rule name (recommended), or an absolute path like "/login". null (default) disables the bounce — every unauthenticated request to a gated route gets a 401. XHR requests always get the 401, never a redirect. The bounce is always a non-cacheable 302.

machine.description: Machine-caller (service-to-service) authentication, since 0.5.25: a request presenting `Authorization: Bearer <key>` matching a configured caller passes the authz gate without a session — it satisfies param.requireAuth, its roles match route param.roles like a session user's, and route policies receive it as { name, roles, machine: true }. Session wins when both are present. A presented-but-invalid key gets a clean 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`, never the login bounce.

enabled.description: Master switch — STRICTLY boolean (any other type refuses to boot). Fail-closed default: no machine caller can authenticate until this is explicitly true.

callers.description: Named machine callers: <callerName> -> { key, roles }. The caller name becomes the audit-trail actor key (records carry machine: true).

key.description: The shared secret this caller presents as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Supports ${secret:KEY} placeholders (resolved from process.env at config load) — prefer them, with long random values (32+ bytes). Compared in constant time against a boot-computed sha256 hash; the raw key is not retained after boot.

roles.description: Roles this caller holds — matched against route param.roles exactly like a session user's roles. Absent = no roles: the caller passes requireAuth-only routes, never role-gated ones (which is also how a route stays human-only: require a role no caller holds).

authenticator.description: Optional custom authenticator: names a <bundle>/authenticators/<name>.js module (the policies/<name>.js shape applied to authN) exporting a SYNCHRONOUS function (req) returning { name, roles } or null. Runs AFTER the built-in caller map (first success wins) and regardless of Bearer presence, so it can verify any sync-checkable credential — a JWT signature, an HMAC header, an x-api-key scheme. A missing, broken or async-function module refuses to boot; at request time a throw or malformed return is fail-closed unauthenticated.

audit.description: Audit trail (#COMPLY2) — a user-attributed, append-only record of "who did what to which record when", written with self.audit(action, data). DISTINCT from lib/logger: the trail has its own store and never rides the log sinks. Boot config: changes need a bundle restart, and every shape here is linted UNCONDITIONALLY (a malformed block refuses the boot even with enabled:false, because an audit trail that is quietly OFF is a failed control). Maps to PCI-DSS req 10, SOC 2 CC7.2, HIPAA §164.312(b).

enabled.description: Master switch — STRICTLY boolean (any other type refuses to boot: a truthy string like "true" would leave the trail silently OFF, which is exactly the failure this lint exists to prevent). When true the store is built and adopted at boot, so an unwritable destination refuses the boot rather than dropping records at the first request. Fail-closed default: false.

file.description: JSONL destination for the default file backend. An absolute path is used as-is; a relative path resolves against the project root, NEVER the process cwd. null (default) means <projectPath>/logs/audit-<bundle>-<env>.jsonl — the per-bundle AND per-env filename is deliberate, so two bundles or two envs never interleave writers into one file. Mutually exclusive with `store`. NOTE: pointing two bundles at the same absolute path defeats that protection and is not detectable at boot, since each bundle lints only its own settings.

store.description: Connector-backed backend: names a connectors.json entry whose .connector supplies core/connectors/<connector>/lib/audit-store.js. Mutually exclusive with `file`. No connector ships an audit-store implementation yet (backends are demand-gated, sqlite first), so setting this today is a clean boot refusal rather than a silent fallback to the file backend — the file backend is the v1 path.

actorKey.description: Which session.user property is snapshotted as the record's actor.key. Only this property plus a COPY of user.roles is stored — never the whole user object, which would leak PII into the trail. The roles copy means a later session mutation cannot retro-edit an already-written record. Machine callers (#MS3) have no session, so their caller NAME is used instead and the record is marked machine:true.

events.description: Framework auto-events — records the framework writes without an explicit self.audit() call.

authz.description: Record every route-authorization denial as an authz.denied record (outcome '401' | 'login-bounce' | '403-roles' | '403-policy' rides in meta.outcome). STRICTLY boolean — any other type refuses to boot, because a truthy non-boolean would not actually opt out. Note that unauthenticated 401s are attacker-triggerable, so this line is attacker-writable in volume, like any log line; throttling is a separate concern.

chain.description: Tamper-evidence hash chain (#COMPLY2 slice 3). When enabled, every record gains a `hash` chaining from its predecessor (HMAC-SHA256 over a canonical form of the record plus the previous hash), verified offline with `gina audit:verify`. Detects post-hoc edit, deletion, insertion or reordering by anyone without the signing key — NOT a defence against the process that writes the records, which holds the key and could forge a whole chain; stream the trail to WORM storage for that adversary. File backend only: a connector `store` is refused, because the chain needs the file store's ordered append. Every shape here is linted UNCONDITIONALLY, like the rest of the audit block.

enabled.description: Master switch for the chain — STRICTLY boolean (any other type refuses to boot: a truthy string like "true" would leave tamper-evidence silently OFF). When true a signing key is required or the boot refuses. Fail-closed default: false.

secret.description: The HMAC signing key. A literal, or a `${secret:VAR}` placeholder resolved at config load — the variable is read from the framework environment first, then `process.env`, so GINA_-prefixed names resolve too (before 0.6.3 the CLI sweep made them unresolvable). Optional here: when omitted the key is read from the GINA_AUDIT_SECRET environment variable. A key shorter than 32 characters boots with a warning. Enabling the chain with no key from either source refuses the boot.

log.description: Logging options for this bundle. Today: `redact` — pre-render log redaction (#B433). Every log message is redacted BEFORE it is rendered and dispatched, so stdout, `gina tail`, the file transport and the Inspector taps all receive the same masked line, and JSON-mode lines cannot be corrupted. ON by default. Boot config: read at config load (the earliest point the block is merged and resolved, so connector-init lines are already covered); changes need a bundle restart. Process-wide: in a merged process (every bundle on one port) the effective rule set is the UNION of every bundle's block; otherwise only the started bundle's block applies.

redact.description: Log redaction rules. A malformed block (unknown key, non-boolean flag, invalid or empty-matching pattern) refuses the boot — a pattern dropped silently is a leak.

enabled.description: Master switch — STRICTLY boolean (a string "false" refuses to boot). Union semantics across a merged process: one bundle enabling redaction is enough for the whole process to redact.

defaults.description: Apply the built-in pattern set: JSON Web Tokens; URL userinfo passwords (`scheme://user:PASSWORD@host`); `Bearer` / `Basic` credentials; named credential query keys (`token`, `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `id_token`, `api_key`/`apikey`, `secret`, `client_secret`, `password`/`passwd`/`pwd`/`passcode`, `auth`, `authorization`, `signature`/`sig`, `otp`, `session_token`) with the key kept and the value masked; api-key style headers (`x-api-key`, `x-auth-token`, …). Deliberately NOT included: a bare long-hex path segment — a content-address key served from storage and an opaque 64-hex credential are the same shape, so add `(?<![0-9a-f])[0-9a-f]{64}(?![0-9a-f])` under `patterns` yourself when your credentials look like that (anchor on the character class — a leading `\b` never fires against a prefixed `key_<hex>` segment). Measured on 433k real log lines: 0 false positives; ~1 µs per line.

secrets.description: Mask, verbatim, every value the secrets resolver substituted for a `${secret:KEY}` placeholder anywhere in this bundle's configs (settings, connectors, routing…) — so a connection string or a connector error can never print a secret. Zero false positives by construction. Values shorter than 8 characters are skipped, with a boot warning naming the config path.

patterns.description: Your own rules, applied to the whole message with the `g` flag (always enforced — without it only the first credential on a line would be masked). String form: a regex source whose whole match becomes `[REDACTED]`. Object form: `{ "pattern": "(sig=)[^&\\s]+", "flags": "gi", "replacement": "$1[REDACTED]", "name": "signed-links" }` — `replacement` follows String.prototype.replace ($1 keeps a group). A pattern that does not compile, or that matches the empty string, refuses the boot. Backtracking behaviour of your own patterns is yours to check.

flags.description: Regex flags; `g` is added when missing

secrets.description: Where `${secret:KEY}` placeholders in this bundle's JSON configs are resolved from. Omit the block entirely and resolution behaves exactly as it always has: the framework environment first, then process.env, failing closed when a key is unset or empty. Declaring it adds a lower-precedence file tier; it never removes or reorders the environment tiers above it.

file.description: One `.env`-style file path, or an array of them, layered UNDERNEATH the environment. Written with the ordinary config tokens, e.g. ["${homedir}/secrets.env", "${homedir}/${scope}/secrets.env"]. A NON-EMPTY environment value always wins: every production delivery mechanism (a Kubernetes envFrom secretRef, an ECS task secret, `sops exec-env`, a CI export) arrives through the environment, so a file that won could let a stale plaintext copy baked into an image silently shadow the credential the platform injected while the bundle looked healthy. As a fallback it can only ever fill a gap. A variable that is SET but EMPTY counts as absent, so the file tier fills it — that is what keeps the common `environment: ["X=${X}"]` passthrough working when the outer variable is unset — but because the same shape also arises when an entrypoint's `export X="$(fetch …)"` fails, the fallback emits a warning naming the key so the dangerous case is visible without the benign one becoming fatal. Within the array, LATER entries win over earlier ones, so a shared base file and a per-scope file combine. A declared file that does not exist contributes nothing and is not an error — a project may ship a base file and add the per-scope one only on some targets. A declared file that EXISTS but cannot be read (wrong permissions or ownership) IS an error and boot refuses, naming the path: skipping it silently would drop the chain onto the shared base file and run the bundle on the wrong credential with no signal. Resolution stays fail-closed when a key is in neither tier. Boot refuses on a non-string, empty or whitespace-only entry, on a `${secret:…}` placeholder (the backend that would resolve it is the one being built), on any `${…}` token the substitution pass did not know — unknown tokens are preserved verbatim by design, so a typo would otherwise become a silent lookup for a literally-named file that never exists — and on a path containing an empty segment (`//`), because such a path does not name the file it appears to — POSIX reads `<a>//<b>` as `<a>/<b>`. The dangerous cause is a `${…}` token that resolved to an EMPTY value: `${homedir}/${scope}/secrets.env` with an empty scope collapses to a read of the file one directory up, silently, with no token left for the check above to catch. The benign cause is a token carrying a trailing slash (e.g. `GINA_HOMEDIR=/opt/gina/`), which resolves to the intended file; the two are indistinguishable by the time the path is assembled, so boot refuses on both rather than risk running on the wrong credential. Removing the doubled separator, or the trailing slash from the token, resolves either. An empty ARRAY is accepted and disables the file tier exactly like `null`, but it warns, because emptying the array to drop one layer drops the whole tier; prefer `null` when opting out deliberately. NOT a secrets-management integration: it does not decrypt, and pointed at ciphertext it yields ciphertext silently. For SOPS, Vault or a KMS keep decrypting at the container entrypoint so values land in the environment, which this tier already prefers. Files are layered once per config-load cycle, so editing one after the bundle has started changes nothing until a restart.

exec.description: One operator-declared command whose stdout supplies the secrets map, layered UNDERNEATH the environment exactly like the `file` tier — a NON-EMPTY environment value always wins, for the same reason: every production delivery mechanism arrives through the environment, and a fetch must never shadow the credential the platform injected. Mutually exclusive with `file`: the two tiers do not layer (no ordering between them has ever been defined), so declaring both refuses the boot — a bundle inheriting a project-wide `file` chain through the shared settings opts out of it with `"file": null` beside its own `exec` block, and `"exec": null` symmetrically drops an inherited exec declaration. The command runs ONCE per bundle per config-load cycle, at boot only, as an argv array with NO shell — element 0 is the binary, resolved through the inherited PATH; ordinary config tokens (`${homedir}`, `${scope}`, `${project}`, …) substitute per element, and an element still carrying an unresolved `${…}` token, or any `${secret:…}` placeholder, refuses the boot. Its stdout MUST be a single flat JSON object of string values — `sops decrypt --output-type json` on a flat secrets file produces it directly; `vault` and `kubectl` need a small wrapper (see the secrets guide's recipes). stdout is the secrets payload and is NEVER echoed into any error, log, or report — a parse failure says so without quoting anything; a non-string value names its key at debug level only. Failure is a per-bundle boot REFUSAL, never a hang: the child is bounded by `timeout` and killed with SIGKILL on expiry (SIGTERM can be ignored by a wedged child, which would hang the boot — the exact failure this bound exists to rule out), and a missing binary, a non-zero exit (the report quotes the last stderr lines, never stdout), a timeout, or malformed output all refuse the boot with the cause named. Pass auth material to the command via environment variables, never argv (argv is visible in `ps`); the child inherits this process's environment because vendor CLIs need their own configuration (`VAULT_ADDR`, `KUBECONFIG`, AWS credentials) — note the CLI sweep moves `GINA_*`/`VENDOR_*`/`USER_*` keys out of `process.env` in CLI and daemon processes, so a fetch command cannot read those there. The platform-native pattern remains BETTER where available — decrypt at the container entrypoint (`sops exec-env`), or inject via the platform (Kubernetes `envFrom` secretRef, ECS task secrets), so values land in the environment this tier already defers to; `exec` exists for environments where the entrypoint cannot be controlled. Secrets fetched here are held in process memory for the lifetime of the process, and rotation needs a restart, exactly as with the other tiers. The `secrets:check` gate runs the SAME command with the SAME timeout to keep its verdict aligned with the boot's, so expect the fetch to run when the gate does. The offline CLI callers that pass no backend (`bundle:mcp-start`, the `connector:*` commands) stay environment-only, as they are for the `file` tier.

command.description: The fetch command, argv form: `["sops", "decrypt", "--output-type", "json", "${project}/secrets.enc.json"]`. No shell is involved — quoting, pipes and redirection are not available; when a pipeline is genuinely needed (`vault kv get -format=json … | jq .data.data`), ship it as a small script file and name that script here.

timeout.description: Milliseconds the fetch may run before the child is SIGKILLed and the boot refuses. The default is deliberately generous for a healthy vendor round-trip while still turning a wedged endpoint into a fast, named failure.

server.description: HTTP server engine and protocol configuration.

engine.description: HTTP server engine. Defaults to "isaac" (built-in HTTP/2 server). "express" uses the project's own express install (the framework deliberately ships no express dependency) — supported range >= 4 < 6, Express 4 and 5 both verified (#B211); an out-of-range major logs a warning at boot.

maxBodySize.description: Enforced ceiling for NON-multipart request bodies (multipart uploads are capped separately by the upload.* settings). A body exceeding it is answered 413 and the stream is destroyed. Accepts B/KB/MB/GB (case-insensitive); a bare number means MB; 0 (or an unparseable value) disables enforcement. Default "64MB" — deliberately permissive: the ceiling exists to stop unbounded growth, not to police payload shapes, and gina's own inter-bundle self.query() hop posts through the same pipeline. New in 0.6.23 (OWASP A10).

maxBodySizeWarn.description: Warn-only companion to maxBodySize: a non-multipart body exceeding it is logged (once per request) but NOT rejected, so the real body-size distribution can be measured before choosing a stricter enforced ceiling. Same unit rules as maxBodySize; 0 disables the warning. Default "2MB". New in 0.6.23 (OWASP A10).

timeout.description: Whole-request socket timeout, in ms or with a unit suffix (e.g. "5m"). Default 0 = unlimited, DELIBERATELY: Server-Sent Events and WebSocket connections are long-lived by design and a finite whole-request clock would kill them, while the slow-body case is already closed by maxBodySize. Set a finite value only if the bundle serves no streaming endpoints. New in 0.6.23.

securityHeaders.description: Framework-level, engine-agnostic security-header emission (new in 0.6.23, OWASP A02). Deliberately NOT the top-level securityHeaders block, which configures the #HDR plugins when a bundle mounts them — the plugins are Express middleware and the default isaac engine never runs the Express chain for HTTP responses, so this block is what actually emits by default. Precedence is first-writer-wins: a header already set by a mounted plugin, an env.json server.response.header entry or an upstream proxy is left untouched. Seven headers are on by default (x-content-type-options, x-download-options, x-permitted-cross-domain-policies, x-xss-protection, referrer-policy, x-dns-prefetch-control, origin-agent-cluster); each can be turned off with "<key>": false. coop/corp are never applied to /_gina/* (deliberately cross-origin).

enabled.description: Master switch. false restores the pre-0.6.23 behaviour (no framework-emitted security headers). Default true.

xFrameOptions.description: Opt-in: emit x-frame-options: SAMEORIGIN. Off by default because it breaks deliberate cross-origin embedding of the app.

coop.description: Opt-in: emit cross-origin-opener-policy: same-origin. Off by default because it severs window.opener and breaks OAuth/payment popup flows. Never applied to /_gina/*.

corp.description: Opt-in: emit cross-origin-resource-policy: same-origin. Off by default because it blocks cross-origin loading of the bundle's assets — including gina's own deliberately cross-origin /_gina/* endpoints, which stay exempt regardless.

hsts.description: Opt-in: emit strict-transport-security: max-age=15552000 (the Hsts plugin's default, 180 days). Off by default because it commits every https visitor's browser for the full period, and per the documented spec deviation it is emitted over plain HTTP too. Mount the Hsts plugin or use env.json for a custom composition — first-writer-wins defers to either.

scheme.description: URL scheme. Use "https" for HTTP/2 (required) or "http" for HTTP/1.1 only.

requireHttps.description: Opt-in transport enforcement. When true, a bundle resolving a cleartext scheme (anything but "https") outside the local scope REFUSES to boot — pre-listen, so the cleartext port is never reachable. Inert in the local scope. Setting it together with allowInsecure is a boot-refused contradiction. Defaults to false: a cleartext bundle outside the local scope warns at boot instead.

allowInsecure.description: The operator's assertion that TLS terminates upstream (service mesh, ingress/load balancer, reverse proxy — the documented h2c topology). When true, the boot-time cleartext-transport warning outside the local scope becomes a single info line. Same vocabulary as mcp.json > server > allowInsecure. Setting it together with requireHttps is a boot-refused contradiction. Defaults to false.

allowHTTP1.description: When true, the HTTP/2 server also accepts HTTP/1.1 connections (ALPN negotiation). Defaults to true.

maintenance.description: Opt-in maintenance mode (#MAINT1). When active, every request EXCEPT the /_gina/* endpoints is answered 503 + Retry-After with a self-contained maintenance page, before static assets, the render/output cache and routing — coverage a route middleware cannot reach, since middleware only runs once a route has matched. The /_gina/* family stays reachable on purpose: liveness keeps answering 200 so an orchestrator does not restart pods over a declared window, and the operator can always reach the toggle. Flip it at runtime with POST /_gina/maintenance (admin-gated); a runtime override is NOT persisted across a restart, so `enabled` here is the durable form. A malformed block warns at boot per key and never refuses a boot.

enabled.description: Master switch, and the state a restart returns to. Must be strictly boolean true to turn maintenance on — any other type or value leaves it off. Defaults to false.

retryAfter.description: Delta-seconds emitted as the Retry-After header on the 503. Integer between 1 and 86400; out-of-range or non-integer values are ignored with a boot warning. Defaults to 300 (5 minutes) — longer than transientErrors' 30s, because an operator-declared window does not resolve in seconds.

message.description: User-facing text shown on the maintenance page and placed in the `explicit` field of the JSON body. HTML-escaped at the emission site. Non-empty string; empty or non-string values are ignored with a boot warning. Defaults to the standard 503 status text (Service Unavailable).

bypassKey.description: Shared secret that lets a chosen visitor through an active maintenance window — the topology-INDEPENDENT bypass, and the only one that works behind a reverse proxy. Present it as the `x-gina-maintenance-key` header (programmatic callers) or as `?gina-maintenance-key=…` once in a browser, which sets a 12h HttpOnly cookie and redirects to the same URL without the secret. Compared in constant time; fail-closed when unset. Supports ${secret:KEY} substitution. Mint with `openssl rand -hex 24`; keys shorter than 16 characters warn at boot. Rotate the key to revoke every outstanding cookie.

allowFrom.description: Supplementary IP allowlist for bypassing an active window. Honoured ONLY for requests that do NOT classify as proxied, because behind a reverse proxy every socket address is the proxy's: an unconditioned list would either admit the entire internet (proxy listed) or nobody (proxy not listed). Behind a proxy this axis is deliberately inert and `bypassKey` is the bypass. Reads req.socket.remoteAddress only — X-Forwarded-For is NOT trusted. Defaults to an empty list (no IP bypass).

transientErrors.description: Opt-in rendering of transient datastore failures as 503 + Retry-After. When enabled, a connector error stamped isTransient that would render as HTTP 500 through throwError renders as 503 with a Retry-After header and a clean user-facing error message instead. Explicit non-500 statuses and permanent errors are never upgraded. A malformed block warns at boot and leaves the feature off — it never refuses a boot.

enabled.description: Master switch. Must be strictly boolean true to turn the upgrade on — any other type or value leaves it off. Defaults to false.

retryAfter.description: Delta-seconds value emitted as the Retry-After header on upgraded 503 responses. Integer between 1 and 86400; out-of-range or non-integer values are ignored with a boot warning. Defaults to 30.

message.description: User-facing text placed in the error field of upgraded 503 responses. Non-empty string; empty or non-string values are ignored with a boot warning. Defaults to the standard 503 status text (Service Unavailable).

warmup.description: List of upstream URLs to pre-establish HTTP/2 sessions at bundle startup. Reduces latency on the first real request.

requireForwardedHeaders.description: Opt-in deterministic proxied-request classification. When true, a request is classified as proxied ONLY when it carries an X-Forwarded-Host header — the port-less-Host heuristic is disabled, so internal calls addressed by service/DNS name (container health probes on app routes, mesh hops, sibling-bundle requests) can no longer rewrite the worker's reverse-proxy host context. Enable only behind a front proxy that always sends X-Forwarded-Host. Defaults to false (historical heuristic: port-less Host OR X-Forwarded-Host).

releaseWatch.description: Stale built-release watch for LOCAL production rehearsals — hard-gated on scope `local` + a non-dev env, never active on a real cluster. When enabled, the bundle watches its SOURCE tree, compares fingerprints against the manifest release stamp, surfaces staleness on GET /_gina/release/status (+ the /_gina/release/events SSE stream) and rebuilds via POST /_gina/release/rebuild with an idle-gated restart (in-flight requests + gina.registerBusyProbe application probes). Fail-closed: disabled by default.

mode.description: notify (default): surface staleness and wait for the operator. auto: rebuild on change automatically — the restart stays idle-gated.

debounceMs.description: Watch-event batch debounce window in ms. Defaults to 750.

reconcileIntervalMs.description: Optional slow re-fingerprint sweep interval in ms for event-lossy mounts; 0 (the default) disables the sweep.

restartMode.description: How a rebuild restarts the process. daemon (default): drain, then spawn `gina bundle:restart` (needs the framework daemon). supervisor: drain, then exit(0) for a container/orchestrator to respawn — the daemonless `gina-container` launch path; requires a restart-on-clean-exit policy (a k8s Deployment or `docker run --restart=always` qualifies; `--restart=on-failure` does not).

idempotency.description: Idempotency-Key request deduplication at the router band (#FIN6), per the IETF draft (draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header). Opt-in TWICE: dormant unless `enabled` is strictly true, AND a route participates only when routing.json declares top-level `idempotency: true` (or `{ "required": true }`, which answers 400 when the header is missing). Runs AFTER route authorization and the rate-limit gate, BEFORE message-schema and DTO validation -- 401 -> 429 -> 409/422/replay -> message validation (when declared) -> 422. The first request bearing an Idempotency-Key reserves the operation (kv `setnx` + the in-flight TTL, crash-safe by expiry) and executes; its rendered JSON response is recorded (status, content-type/location headers, body, payload fingerprint) under the retention TTL, and a retry with the same key + payload is answered with the RECORDED response plus `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. A duplicate while the original is in flight gets 409 + Retry-After; the same key with a DIFFERENT payload gets 422. Requests with NO resolvable principal (no session user, no machine caller) are SKIPPED -- a stored response must never cross principals. Responses >= 500, bodies over `maxBodySize`, and any response that never passes through renderJSON (a template render, a redirect, an error egress) RELEASE the reservation so retries re-execute. Deduplication SCOPE follows the kv namespace's backend: in-memory dedups per process (a retry on another replica re-executes -- the resolver warns); replica-safe dedup needs a redis- or sqlite-backed namespace. Outage policy is the namespace's own `failMode`: `open` proceeds without dedup, `closed` answers 503 + Retry-After. Folded from settings.json into the runtime server block (env.json keys win); resolved once at engine start, so changes need a bundle restart. Structurally invalid values on an enabled block refuse the boot.

enabled.description: Arm the dedup gate. Must be strictly true; any other value (including the string "true") leaves it dormant.

namespace.description: The kv namespace holding reservations and recorded response envelopes. Must be DECLARED under `kv.namespaces` -- an undeclared name refuses the boot. Give it its OWN namespace: its `failMode` is then unambiguously the dedup outage policy.

keyField.description: The `session.user` property that identifies a signed-in caller (machine callers key on their registered name automatically) -- the same convention as `server.rateLimit.keyField`.

ttl.description: Retention of a recorded response envelope (duration string or ms). A retry inside this window replays the recorded response; after expiry the operation re-executes. Publish this policy to your API consumers, per the draft.

inflightTtl.description: Lifetime of the in-flight reservation. A crashed process's reservation self-releases after this window, letting a retry re-execute. Size it above your slowest opted-in request.

maxBodySize.description: Largest response body (bytes) stored for replay. A larger response releases the reservation instead -- the retry re-executes.

retryAfter.description: The Retry-After value answered on 409 (in-flight duplicate) and 503 (store outage on a failMode `closed` namespace).

rateLimit.description: Identified-caller quota enforcement at the router band (#MS6). Opt-in: dormant unless `enabled` is strictly true. Runs AFTER route authorization (the principal resolver) and BEFORE the validation tier (message-schema, then DTO), so the order is 401 -> 429 -> 422; a request with NO resolvable principal (no session user, no machine caller) is SKIPPED, never bucketed -- anonymous flood control belongs to the edge proxy and the HTTP/2 rapid-reset guard, not here. Fixed-window counters live in the kv namespace this block names, so choosing the namespace's backend chooses the quota's SCOPE: in-memory counts per process; replica-shared quotas need a redis- or sqlite-backed namespace (the resolver warns about a memory backend, and about a redis entry missing `enableOfflineQueue: false` + `commandTimeout` -- with ioredis defaults an outage QUEUES gated requests instead of degrading). Outage policy is the namespace's own `failMode`: `open` allows without headers, `closed` answers 503 + Retry-After. Denials answer 429 + Retry-After plus the draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-11 structured fields (`RateLimit`, `RateLimit-Policy`); allowed limited requests carry them too (without `t`). Per-route overrides ride routing.json's top-level `rateLimit` key (`false` = exempt; `{limit, window}` REPLACES the default for that route in its own bucket). Folded from settings.json into the runtime server block (env.json keys win); resolved once at engine start, so changes need a bundle restart. Structurally invalid values on an enabled block refuse the boot.

enabled.description: Arm the quota gate. Must be strictly true; any other value (including the string "true") leaves it dormant.

namespace.description: The kv namespace holding the counters. Must be DECLARED under `kv.namespaces` -- an undeclared name refuses the boot. Give the limiter its OWN namespace: its `failMode` is then unambiguously the limiter's outage policy.

keyField.description: The `session.user` property that identifies a signed-in caller (e.g. "id"). Required because the session user is app-owned shape -- a guessed default would mis-key silently. Machine callers (#MS3) key on their registered name automatically; a user record where this field is absent/empty is unidentified and SKIPPED.

limit.description: Requests allowed per principal per window (the default policy). A structurally invalid value on an enabled block refuses the boot.

window.description: Window length. Accepts "1m", "30s", "500ms" or a number of milliseconds; must be positive. An unparseable value on an enabled block refuses the boot.

query.description: Outbound client policy for Controller::query(). Folded from settings.json into the runtime server block (env.json keys win, settings.json fills what env.json lacks).

circuitBreaker.description: Per-authority circuit breaker for query() (#MS5). Opt-in: dormant unless `enabled` is strictly true. Gates BOTH client paths (HTTP/1.x and HTTP/2) above the protocol dispatch, so an open circuit rejects with a machine-readable CIRCUIT_OPEN error (status 503, retryable false) before any connection, retry or pre-flight attempt. State is per `hostname:port`, lives on the engine instance (resets on bundle restart) and transitions closed -> open -> half-open lazily, with a single critical-request probe per cooldown. Config changes need a bundle restart (resolved once at engine start).

enabled.description: Arm the breaker. Must be strictly true; any other value (including the string "true") leaves it dormant.

failureThreshold.description: Consecutive transport-class failures (per authority, after each call's own retries are exhausted) that open the circuit. A structurally invalid value on an enabled block refuses the boot.

cooldown.description: How long an open circuit rejects before admitting one half-open probe. Accepts "30s", "500ms", "1m" or a number of milliseconds; an unparseable value on an enabled block refuses the boot.

cache.description: Bundle-wide render/output-cache defaults. `type` / `store` here are folded into the runtime `server.cache` (which also carries the per-env `enable` / `path` / `ttl` / `maxEntries` from env.json), so they act as the default a route inherits when its own `cache` omits them.

type.description: Bundle-wide default cache strategy. A per-route `cache.type` overrides it; a route with `cache` set but no `type` inherits it. `memory` = in-process (volatile); `fs` = disk-backed (restart-surviving); `redis` = shared L2 across replicas + per-replica L1.

store.description: Required for `redis`: the name of a `connectors.json` entry ({ "<name>": { "connector": "redis", "host": …, "port": … } }) providing the L2 connection. Ignored for memory / fs.

name.description: Optional RFC 9211 Cache-Status identifier for this bundle's render/output cache (default `gina-cache`). Grammar is a conservative RFC 8941 token subset: a letter, then up to 63 of [A-Za-z0-9._-]. An invalid value is ignored with a boot warn. When `server.hidePoweredBy` is true and the cache is enabled, leaving it unset logs a boot warn naming the disclosure — set any token (e.g. `cache`) to close it, or explicitly `gina-cache` to keep the default wire and silence the warn.

session.description: Session plugin defaults (#CSRF1, #COMPLY4) — cookie flags and the absolute-timeout cap the gina.plugins.Session() wrapper applies at factory-call time. Options set explicitly in bundle code always win. Boot config: changes need a bundle restart. The session-record TTL is NOT set here — it comes from the store's connectors.json entry or constructor options, and follows the cookie maxAge when neither is set.

absoluteTimeout.description: Absolute session cap in MILLISECONDS, measured from login (the anchor req.login() stamps at session-id rotation; manually-bound sessions are anchored one request later). Opt-in: when set, an authenticated session older than this is destroyed on its next request — regardless of activity — and the request proceeds with a fresh anonymous session. Bundle code passing session({ absoluteTimeout }) wins over this default; absoluteTimeout: false in bundle code disables it. Composes with idle expiry: the cookie maxAge and the store-record TTL roll with activity, this cap does not.

cookie.description: Defaults for the express-session cookie object. Only these three flags are read from settings; every other cookie option (maxAge, path, domain, ...) is passed in bundle code.

sameSite.description: SameSite default. Matched case-insensitively at runtime; use the lowercase canonical form. "none" requires secure=true (browser-parity invariant, refused at factory call time otherwise).

httpOnly.description: HttpOnly default — keeps the session cookie out of document.cookie.

secure.description: Secure default: true, false, or "auto" (express-session derives the flag from the connection scheme). SameSite=None with secure not strictly true refuses at factory call time.

integrationMode.description: How Socket.io attaches to the HTTP server.

pingTimeout.description: Time to wait for a pong before considering the connection dropped (e.g. "10s", "20s").

upload.description: File upload configuration (multipart/form-data). A file part's Content-Disposition group="…" parameter selects its upload group; a part with no or an empty group resolves to `untagged`, and a group not configured under `groups` is rejected with HTTP 400 before anything touches disk. `additionalProperties` stays true DELIBERATELY: applications may keep their own per-group keys (composed app-side), and this schema documents what the FRAMEWORK reads — a key not listed here has no framework behaviour.

tmpPath.description: Global parse-time landing directory for uploaded files (supports ${tmpPath}, which resolves to <project>/tmp). Landing-dir fallback chain: uploadDir, then tmpPath, then the OS temp dir.

uploadDir.description: Alternative global landing directory; wins over tmpPath when both are set.

maxFieldsSize.description: WHOLE-REQUEST size cap, compared against the request Content-Length (HTTP 431 past it). Unit-suffixed string (B/KB/MB/GB); a bare number means MB. 0 or unset disables. Block-level only — a per-group override has no framework behaviour.

maxFields.description: Per-request FILE-COUNT cap (HTTP 400 past it). 0 or unset disables. Block-level only.

maxTextFields.description: Maximum multipart TEXT (non-file) fields per request (HTTP 400 past the cap). Default 1000; 0 or below means no limit.

maxTextFieldSize.description: Per text-field size cap (HTTP 400 on a truncated field). Unit-suffixed string; a bare number means MB. Default 1MB; explicit 0 disables.

autoTmpCleanupTimeout.description: Arms a per-file deletion timer at parse time for each landed file (e.g. "30s", "10m", "1h", "500ms"; a bare number is milliseconds). false, 0 or empty disables it — the shipped default. Block-level only. When armed, a boot-time sweep also reclaims staged parts (<32 hex>.part) a previous process stranded — parts older than this timeout (floored at 1h) in the configured landing directories; disabled means no sweep, and removing staged files is then the operator's own job. The sweep logs at info level only what it removed (or errors); a boot that finds nothing older than the threshold logs at debug, so a silent boot at the default info level is a no-op, not a skipped sweep.

groups.description: Named upload groups — at least one is required to enable uploads. A file is checked against its group's rules at parse time. `untagged` is a NORMAL configured group serving every part that carries no group tag; it obeys its own configuration.

additionalProperties.description: One upload group. Keys beyond these are ignored by the framework (applications may compose their own app-side).

path.description: Parse-time landing directory for this group's files, overriding the global default (created if missing, crash-guarded). For a driver-routed group this is ONLY the staging dir — the driver owns final placement, and a path inside the driver's root earns a boot warning.

allowedExtensions.description: "*" accepts every extension; an array (e.g. ["jpg","png"]) rejects any other extension with HTTP 400 at parse time.

isMultipleAllowed.description: When explicitly false, a request carrying more than one file for this group is rejected with HTTP 400. OMITTED means multiple files are allowed — the permissive default.

driver.description: #STO1 (slice 1) — route this group's self.store() step through the named settings.storage driver: files publish as opaque storage keys (result entries carry key/group/driver and the layer's on-disk size, no filename) instead of moving to the call's target directory. A driver not defined in storage.drivers refuses the boot. The parse/staging path is unchanged.

simulateWriteError.description: TEST-ONLY fault injector (#B144): every upload tagged with this group fails deterministically with a guarded 500 through the real write-error path, so the crash-guard can be probed on your own upload surface after a pickup. Ignored in production scope; a boot warning names it either way.

kv.description: General-purpose key-value primitive (#KV1) — strict-declared NAMESPACES reached from application code as gina.kv('<name>') / gina.kv(). Values are JSON-serialized; null and undefined are refused on every write (a stored null would be indistinguishable from a miss). TTLs are MILLISECONDS and must be positive — ttl: 0 refuses rather than meaning no-expiry. Namespaces are process-global, read once at boot from the STARTING bundle's settings; the whole feature is dormant when this block is absent, and gina.kv() then throws a named error. Deliberately NOT a redis client: no data structures, no batch ops, no key scanning, no binary values.

default.description: Namespace returned by a no-argument gina.kv(). Must name an entry in `namespaces` — a default pointing at an undeclared namespace refuses the boot. Omit it and every call must name its namespace explicitly.

namespaces.description: KV namespaces, keyed by name (^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$). Each namespace owns its backend and failure policy; {} declares a plain in-memory namespace. Unknown per-namespace keys are ignored with a boot warning naming them, because a silently-dropped key reads as configured behaviour that never happens.

store.description: connectors.json entry name backing this namespace. The entry's `connector` field selects the implementation (core/connectors/<connector>/lib/kv-store.js); a connector without one refuses the boot rather than degrading silently to memory. Omit for the in-memory backend. The redis connector (shared across hosts) and the sqlite connector (zero-dependency, durable, shared across processes on one host) both implement one; the others arrive demand-first.

failMode.description: Backend-error policy. closed (default): a backend error rejects the call. open: every op degrades to its miss-shaped result with a warning — for cache-like namespaces where availability beats consistency. Consulted on backend errors only (validation errors always reject); the in-memory backend does not error, so the knob becomes operative with connector-backed stores.

sweepInterval.description: Milliseconds between expired-entry sweeps for the in-memory backend (default 30000). Expired entries are also dropped lazily on read, so the sweep bounds memory, not correctness.

storage.description: Pluggable object storage (#STO1) — an adapter (where bytes live) crossed with a strategy (how keys are laid out), behind one callback-shaped contract. Reached from application code as gina.storage() / gina.storage('<name>'). Keys are OPAQUE: store the key a put() returns, never parse or compose one. Boot config — changes need a bundle restart, and every shape here is linted UNCONDITIONALLY, because unlike a cache a storage layer has no safe degraded mode: a driver that cannot build would leave put() writing nowhere. Since slice 1 an upload group may route its self.store() step through a driver (upload.groups.<name>.driver); the multipart parse/staging path is otherwise untouched.

default.description: Name of the driver returned by a no-argument gina.storage(). Must name an entry in `drivers` — a default pointing at a driver that does not exist refuses the boot rather than failing at the first put(). Omit it and every call must name its driver explicitly.

drivers.description: Storage drivers, keyed by name. Nested under their own key (rather than sitting directly under `storage`) so a driver may legitimately be called "default", and so future block-level options never reserve a driver name — the same shape `upload.groups` uses.

^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$.description: One storage driver. Unknown keys are ignored with a boot warning naming them, because a silently-dropped key reads as configured behaviour that never happens.

adapter.description: Where the bytes live. `local` = the local filesystem under `root`. `s3` = any S3-compatible provider (AWS S3, Scaleway, MinIO, R2…), STORELESS: the provider carries each object's metadata on the object itself (immutable after upload, like the key), so there is no `root`, no `store` and no tiering — and the SDK (@aws-sdk/client-s3 + @aws-sdk/lib-storage + @aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner) is the PROJECT's dependency, never the framework's — the same policy every database connector follows. A configured s3 driver whose SDK is not installed refuses the boot with the npm install hint.

strategy.description: How keys are laid out. `sharded` = YYYY/MM/DD/<ulid><ext>, which keeps directories small enough to list and — because a ULID sorts by creation time — keeps entries within a day ordered. `cas` = content-addressed (blobs/<algo>/<aa>/<bb>/<hex>, extension-less): identical bytes stored twice yield the SAME key with a reference count of 2, release() drops a reference, and a periodic sweep collects blobs that have sat at zero past a grace window — built for immutable content (in-place mutation is impossible by construction; editing mints a new blob and key). `stream` = one directory per asset (assets/<ulid>/original<ext>), built for large sequential media: it adds RESUMABLE uploads (createUpload / writeSegment / statUpload / finalize / abortUpload, capabilities.resumable true), segments may arrive out of order and are written positionally so no assembly pass runs at finalise, and finalise verifies coverage as an interval UNION before publishing — a hole in a sparse file reads back as zeros, so an unverified publish would be silently corrupt. It neither tiers nor hashes, so inlineThreshold and hash are ignored (with a warning) there. Keys are OPAQUE under every strategy — changing a driver's strategy on populated storage is a re-key migration, not a config edit, and the boot warns when the configured strategy stops matching the one stamped on the root. Under the `s3` adapter only `sharded` runs — the provider owns placement, so the layout algorithm collapses to key naming — and it is the default there: omit `strategy` entirely on an s3 driver.

root.description: Absolute directory holding this driver's objects. MUST be absolute — a relative root would resolve against the process cwd, which depends on how the bundle was launched. MUST NOT sit inside any bundle's web-served tree (its publicPath, or any content.statics target): objects there would be directly fetchable without passing any authorization, and so would the driver's own metadata database, which lives at <root>/.meta.db. Both conditions refuse the boot.

bucket.description: s3 only, REQUIRED there: the bucket name. The opaque keys this layer mints live under `prefix` inside it — the bucket is provider identity, exactly as `root` is filesystem identity for `local`.

region.description: s3 only: the signing region. Omit it on real AWS to let the SDK's own chain (env vars / shared config) resolve it; when a custom `endpoint` is configured and no region is set, the S3-compat convention `us-east-1` is used — most compatible providers accept any region string.

endpoint.description: s3 only: an S3-compatible endpoint for non-AWS providers (e.g. "s3.fr-par.scw.cloud", a MinIO host). `https://` is prepended when no scheme is given. Omit for AWS itself.

prefix.description: s3 only: key prefix inside the bucket (a trailing `/` is added when missing), namespacing this driver in a shared bucket. Relative only — no leading `/`, no `..`. The OPAQUE key excludes it: re-pointing `prefix` orphans previously stored objects exactly as re-pointing a local `root` does.

accessKeyId.description: s3 only: static credential id — set BOTH accessKeyId and secretAccessKey or NEITHER. Omit both (recommended on AWS/k8s) and the SDK default provider chain runs: env vars, shared config, IMDS, IRSA. The anchored ${secret:KEY} form is substituted at config load, so credentials need not live in the file.

secretAccessKey.description: s3 only: static credential secret — see accessKeyId; ${secret:KEY} recommended over a literal.

sessionToken.description: s3 only: session token for temporary static credentials; meaningful only beside the accessKeyId/secretAccessKey pair (ignored with a boot warning otherwise — the SDK chain supplies its own session credentials).

forcePathStyle.description: s3 only: path-style addressing (https://endpoint/bucket/key rather than virtual-hosted) — required by MinIO and some self-hosted providers.

presignExpiry.description: s3 only: presigned-URL lifetime as a UNIT-SUFFIXED duration ("15m", "1h"). resolve() and serveFromStorage()'s offload redirect mint URLs with this lifetime; a transfer already in flight survives expiry (the signature is validated at request time). Not a caching knob — the serving facade re-presigns per request.

maxObjectSize.description: Per-object byte ceiling, as a UNIT-SUFFIXED string ("50MB", "512KB", "1.5GB"). A bare number is refused with a boot warning and the default applies — deliberately stricter than settings.upload, where a bare number means megabytes for back-compat. There is no house meaning to inherit: `upload` already reads a bare number as a count (maxFields) in one key and as megabytes (maxFieldsSize) in another, so this key refuses to guess. Defense in depth: no per-file cap exists upstream today, only whole-request caps.

store.description: Connector-backed metadata store: names a connectors.json entry whose .connector supplies core/connectors/<connector>/lib/storage-store.js. Omit it (the default) and metadata goes to an embedded SQLite file at <root>/.meta.db, which is documented SINGLE-PROCESS per root — SQLite locking on a shared network filesystem is a known-broken story, so two bundles or replicas sharing one root need a connector-backed store instead. The `couchbase` connector ships one; a connector that does not is a clean boot refusal rather than a silent fallback to the embedded file. Since size tiering, rows may carry the object PAYLOAD itself (objects under inlineThreshold), so the store needs binary-safe fields and losing it loses those objects, not just their metadata.

inlineThreshold.description: Size-tiering threshold, as a UNIT-SUFFIXED string ("64KB") — objects strictly UNDER it are stored inline in the metadata store (one transaction, no filesystem round-trip; resolve() answers {kind:'inline'} and capabilities.inline is true); at or above it they take the temp+rename file path. "0B" disables tiering for this driver, keeping every object a visible dated file. A unit-less value warns at boot and the default applies. The 64KB default is the measured knee on the embedded store (inline puts 2.7-13x faster at or under it, destabilizing above). Changing it is retroactively safe: reads follow where each object's bytes actually live, so existing objects stay readable on either side. Operational tradeoffs to weigh: sub-threshold objects are not individually visible on disk (they live inside .meta.db, which any root-level backup still carries), and on a connector-backed store the payloads land in that backend. Applies to `sharded` and `cas` alike; ignored (with a warning) under `stream`, where a multi-gigabyte object has no business living in a metadata row.

hash.description: cas only — the digest algorithm whose name becomes a path segment in every key (blobs/<hash>/…). Validated at boot against THIS runtime's crypto.getHashes(): an unavailable name refuses the boot (sha256 and sha512 exist on both supported runtimes; blake2b512 is Node-only — measured). Changing it later is ADDITIVE, never a re-key: existing blobs stay addressable under their own namespace, new writes land under the new one, dedup does not span the two, and the boot notes the change once. Ignored (with a warning) under `sharded` and `stream`, neither of which hashes.

fsync.description: cas and stream — whether writes are fsynced before they are published or acknowledged: under `cas`, the temp file before rename(2) (hard — a failure fails the put) and the parent directory after it (best-effort — platforms that cannot fsync a directory, e.g. Windows and some network mounts, skip it silently); under `stream`, additionally each resumable SEGMENT before its durability marker is written, which is what makes a marker imply durable bytes. Defaults ON in both: cas exists for immutable/legal content where an acknowledged write must survive power loss, and a resumable upload's whole contract is that a range the client was told is durable actually is. `false` opts back into the sharded-class durability (atomic rename, recent writes at risk on host crash) — measured, the per-segment cost is ~2% of network-paced ingest at 100 Mbps but fsync-dominant on a 10 Gbps LAN, which is when to consider it. Ignored (with a warning) under `sharded`, whose writes never fsync.

sweepInterval.description: cas only — how often the garbage-collection sweep runs, as a UNIT-SUFFIXED duration string (ms/s/m/h/d, e.g. "15m"). The sweep collects blobs whose reference count has sat at zero for longer than sweepGrace: release() itself never deletes bytes. "0s" disables the periodic sweep for this driver (references still count; nothing is ever collected until a sweep runs). A unit-less value warns at boot and the default applies. The default is a reasoned reclaim-latency bound, not a benchmark.

sweepGrace.description: Age gate for reclaiming abandoned write residue, as a UNIT-SUFFIXED duration string (e.g. "1h") — what it ages depends on the driver. `cas`: BOTH how long a blob must have sat at ZERO references before the sweep may collect it AND how old a crashed-put temp must be before build-time reclamation. `sharded`: the crashed-put temp cutoff alone (it sweeps at build, never on a tick). `s3`: how old an incomplete multipart upload must be before the build-time sweep aborts it (an incomplete upload bills storage until aborted). The grace window is a correctness margin, not a convenience: it keeps every sweep from racing in-flight work (under cas, re-uploading just-released content within the window is free — the blob is resurrected, no bytes transferred twice). Must be greater than zero; zero or unit-less values warn at boot and the default applies. Reasoned default: comfortably longer than any plausible in-flight upload.

chunkSize.description: stream only — the segment size the write path is tuned for, as a UNIT-SUFFIXED string ("8MB"). It becomes the write stream's highWaterMark (the same syscall size with no hand-rolled buffer and no extra copy) and is echoed back by createUpload() so a client can size its segments to match. A client may still send any segment size; this is a tuning knob, not a protocol constraint. A unit-less or zero value warns at boot and the default applies. NOTE gina neither prevents nor can prevent fragmentation: Node exposes no fallocate binding and ftruncate produces a fully SPARSE file, so contiguity is a filesystem/volume concern (XFS extent hints and the like), never something this key buys. Ignored (with a warning) under `sharded` and `cas`.

sessionTtl.description: stream only — how long an untouched resumable upload session survives before the sweep reclaims it, as a UNIT-SUFFIXED duration string (ms/s/m/h/d, e.g. "24h"). Liveness is the mtime of the session's assembling file, which advances on every segment write — not the session directory's, which only moves when entries are added or removed. The same gate also reclaims temp files left by a crashed put(). Must be greater than zero: a zero TTL would reclaim uploads that are still being written to, so zero and unit-less values warn at boot and the default applies. Reasoned default, not a benchmark: a paused-then-resumed upload over a bad link must comfortably fit inside it.

sessionSweepInterval.description: stream only — how often the abandoned-session sweep runs, as a UNIT-SUFFIXED duration string (e.g. "1h"). A pass also runs at driver BUILD, which is what reclaims whatever a crashed process left behind; the timer is unref'd and never holds the process open. "0s" disables the periodic sweep for this driver (the build-time pass still runs). A unit-less value warns at boot and the default applies. There is no operator door for this sweep in this release — `storage:gc` and POST /_gina/storage/gc stay cas-only.

response.description: HTTP response header overrides, typically used for CORS.

header.description: Static response headers added to every response from this bundle.

swig.description: Opt-in override for the swig template engine. When useProject is true the bundle loads the project-pinned package from the project's node_modules instead of the framework's bundled copy — provided the project version satisfies the framework's same-major and minimum-version constraint. A rejected override falls back to the framework copy and logs a warning at bundle startup.

useProject.description: When true, attempt to load the package from <projectPath>/node_modules. When false or omitted, always load the framework's bundled copy (default, current behaviour).

package.description: npm package name to resolve. Defaults to @rhinostone/swig (native swig syntax). Set to @rhinostone/swig-twig to use the Twig-syntax frontend. The abandoned upstream "swig" name is never accepted.

autoescape.description: Whether swig auto-escapes variable output (`{{ x }}`) by default, passed to swig.setDefaults({ autoescape }). Defaults to false today; set true to HTML-escape variable output as an XSS defense — nunjucks defaults to true (see settings.nunjucks.autoescape).

template.description: Per-engine custom template loader (async loader extension point). When a loader is configured the engine resolves templates through it instead of the local filesystem, enabling remote / CDN / object-storage / in-memory template backends. Bundles without a loader render from disk exactly as before.

loader.description: Custom async loader for the swig render path. Mirrors the connectors.json convention: a named built-in `type` plus type-specific flat keys. When present, the bundle renders via the isolated per-bundle swig engine (controller.render-swig-async.js) instead of the filesystem path.

type.description: Built-in loader name. "memory" loads templates from an inline `templates` map (no network or filesystem). "http" fetches templates over HTTP(S) from a configured origin + basePath, with a TTL'd source cache and opt-in ETag revalidation.

templates.description: For type "memory": flat map of template identifier to source string.

origin.description: For type "http": scheme://host[:port] of the template origin (no path). http or https. Required for the http loader.

basePath.description: For type "http": path prefix under origin that template identifiers resolve against (root-relative, flat namespace). Defaults to "". Resolved URLs are containment-checked to stay under origin+basePath.

ttl.description: For type "http": source-cache TTL in seconds (absolute from fetch). Defaults to 60. Raise it for immutable CDN-published templates; 0 caches until evicted.

revalidate.description: For type "http": when true, a cache hit issues a conditional GET (If-None-Match) and serves cached source on 304, refreshing the TTL. Off by default (no per-hit round-trip). Turn on for live-CMS templates whose origin emits ETags.

cache.description: #TPL1 Tier-2 opt-in: reuse compiled templates across requests via the shared per-bundle engine + AsyncLocalStorage per-request context. Off by default (per-request render, no compiled-template reuse). Force-disabled in dev mode regardless so template edits are picked up live without a restart.

loader.description: Custom async loader for the nunjucks render path. Mirrors the connectors.json convention: a named built-in `type` plus type-specific flat keys. When present, the bundle renders via a per-request nunjucks Environment over this loader (controller.render-nunjucks-async.js) instead of the cached-Environment filesystem path.

type.description: Built-in loader name. "memory" loads templates from an inline `templates` map (no network or filesystem). "http" fetches templates over HTTP(S) from a configured origin + basePath, with a TTL'd source cache and opt-in ETag revalidation.

templates.description: For type "memory": flat map of template identifier to source string.

origin.description: For type "http": scheme://host[:port] of the template origin (no path). http or https. Required for the http loader.

basePath.description: For type "http": path prefix under origin that template identifiers resolve against (root-relative, flat namespace). Defaults to "". Resolved URLs are containment-checked to stay under origin+basePath.

ttl.description: For type "http": source-cache TTL in seconds (absolute from fetch). Defaults to 60. Raise it for immutable CDN-published templates; 0 caches until evicted.

revalidate.description: For type "http": when true, a cache hit issues a conditional GET (If-None-Match) and serves cached source on 304, refreshing the TTL. Off by default (no per-hit round-trip). Turn on for live-CMS templates whose origin emits ETags.

cache.description: #TPL1 Tier-2 opt-in: reuse compiled templates across requests via a shared per-request-context (AsyncLocalStorage) nunjucks Environment. Off by default (per-request Environment, no compiled-template reuse). Force-disabled in dev mode regardless so template edits are picked up live without a restart.

render.description: Template engine dispatch. Selects which delegate file (controller.render-swig.js or controller.render-nunjucks.js) handles self.render() calls for this bundle. Switching to "nunjucks" requires `npm install nunjucks` in the project root — the framework does not bundle nunjucks.

engine.description: Bundle-level template engine for self.render() HTML output. "swig" (default) uses @rhinostone/swig via controller.render-swig.js; "nunjucks" uses the project-installed nunjucks package via controller.render-nunjucks.js. When set to "nunjucks", bundle startup fails with NUNJUCKS_NOT_INSTALLED if the package is absent from the project's node_modules. An explicit template extension overrides this per render: a section whose templates.json `ext` is ".njk" (or a self.setTemplate(file, '.njk') call) renders through nunjucks, ".swig" through swig — so a single bundle can mix engines; ".html" and any other extension follow this setting.

emitTimeout.description: Opt-in bound, in milliseconds, on a call to an emit-style entity method that never signals completion (it neither emits its `<shortName>#<method>` trigger nor returns a Promise that settles). When exceeded, that call alone rejects with an Error naming the trigger, a warn line is logged, and its pending slot is released so later calls are unaffected. Absent or 0 (the default): no bound — a call that never completes stays pending, as it did before 0.6.20. Set it above the slowest legitimate operation in the bundle (bulk operations included); it applies to every entity of the bundle and is read once at startup.

getConfig.description: How `self.getConfig()` hands configuration to application code.

mode.description: `view` (the default): each call returns a private copy-on-write view over the live configuration — reads copy nothing, a write lands in the view's own overlay and never reaches the live configuration or another call, and the first enumeration of a node (Object.keys, JSON.stringify, for…in, spread) copies that subtree once. Three things a deep clone allowed do not work on a node you have not enumerated: structuredClone() throws a DataCloneError, Object.freeze() / seal() throw a TypeError, and console.log() / util.inspect() show the live values instead of your writes (property reads and JSON.stringify are truthful). `clone`: every call deep-copies the requested configuration — the behaviour before this setting existed, and the opt-out for code that relies on one of those three. Read on every call, so a change applies on the next request in development and at the next restart in production.

nunjucks.description: Configuration for the nunjucks template engine (when render.engine is "nunjucks"). The package is never framework-bundled — it must exist in the project's node_modules.

package.description: npm package name to resolve in <projectPath>/node_modules. Defaults to "nunjucks" (upstream).

autoescape.description: Whether the nunjucks Environment autoescapes by default. Passed to `new nunjucks.Environment(loader, { autoescape })`.
